name: Distribution-steered sampling codes
definition: The message is embedded in how each symbol is sampled from a model's distribution, for example in the random number used to sample, and the receiver recovers it from the distribution or the randomness.
notes: Access differs between children and between sender and receiver (guo_2026:shared-seed-access, pang_2026:draft-model-public-only, zamir_2024:decoder-distribution-agnostic); see access_needed. Not every child preserves the cover distribution.

name: Rejection sampling
definition: Channel samples are drawn until a keyed or public function of one equals the next message bit; in the bounded form at most a fixed number of draws is made, trying to find a match.

name: Keyed, bounded rejection sampling
definition: For each bit, at most two channel blocks are drawn, looking for one whose keyed pseudorandom function value F_K(N, c) equals the bit; the protocol is stateful.
notes: Hopper Construction 1; credited to Anderson and Petitcolas.

name: Rejection sampling with a public unbiased function
definition: A public function, assumed unbiased on the channel, decides whether a sampled block carries the next bit; the assumption does not hold for every channel.
notes: Hopper Construction 2.

name: Shared-sample robust coding
definition: Channel draws made with pseudorandom inputs that sender and receiver share stand in for shared blocks and lower the decoding error, so that robust hiding is possible against any admissible warden relation.
notes: Hopper Construction 3; impractical by its authors' account. Not rejection sampling (Review B).

name: Keyed function of a robust document feature
definition: A keyed function f picks the shingle of each document that maximises it, giving a protocol robust against a particular class of edits on text-like channels.
notes: Hopper Construction 4. The quote omits the unbiased function that carries the bit (Review B), so treat it as a broad neighbour.

name: Partition codes
definition: The symbol space is split into groups and the message chooses the group from which the next symbol is drawn.

name: Fixed shared bins
definition: A shared random partition of the vocabulary into equal-sized bins lets the bin of each token carry a fixed-length block of ciphertext.
notes: Heavily modifies the output distribution (kaptchuk_2021:nlp-schemes-insecure). A random hyperplane split is not this code: see m-hyperplane-buckets.

name: Hyperplane buckets
definition: A random hyperplane in the embedding space splits the vocabulary into two buckets, and each output token carries one bit by the bucket it falls in.
notes: Not equal-sized random bins (X).

name: Near-equiprobable partition
definition: The cover space is split into parts of approximately equal probability mass and the message bit picks the part to sample from.

name: Recursive near-equiprobable grouping
definition: At each step the vocabulary is grouped adaptively into groups of approximately equal probability, the message chooses a group, and the operation repeats within it.
notes: The multi-bit form of the balanced partition (Review A, cross-link).

name: Prefix-code (Huffman) sampling
definition: A prefix code built from the model's distribution at each step is walked by the message bits to choose a token.
notes: Shares its grounding with m-huffman-every-step.

name: Huffman at every step
definition: A Huffman code over the vocabulary is rebuilt at every step and followed bit by bit from the root to a leaf token.

name: Thresholded (patient) Huffman
definition: The Huffman code is used only at steps where its total variation distance from the model's distribution is small enough; otherwise the step samples from the model and waits.

name: Interval (range or arithmetic) coding
definition: The message, read as a number, is decoded into symbols by partitioning a range in proportion to the model's probabilities: arithmetic coding run in reverse.
notes: One mechanism over Markov and neural cover models (both reviews); the cover model is an attribute, not a different mechanism.

name: Plain range partition over a fixed model
definition: At each step the range is partitioned to match the model's outbound probabilities and the symbol whose subrange contains the message number is emitted.
notes: Holds both Moraldo's Markov chain and Ziegler's neural LM.

name: Interval coding with per-step truncation
definition: Arithmetic coding over a neural LM in which the number of candidate tokens kept, fixed in earlier work, is re-chosen at each step.

name: Keyed sampling-randomness embedding
definition: Message bits stand in for the random number used to sample each token, masked afresh at every sampling event by a generator keyed with state the two parties share.
notes: Meteor; its rate follows the step's entropy (kaptchuk_2021:approach-meteor).

name: Coupling codes
definition: Ciphertext that looks uniformly random is joined to the cover distribution by a coupling, so the published symbol follows the cover distribution.

name: Minimum-entropy coupling
definition: An iterative minimum-entropy coupling joins uniform ciphertext to an autoregressively specified cover distribution.
notes: iMEC.

name: Maximal coupling through a public draft model
definition: A small public draft model that both parties run on the public transcript partitions the vocabulary into buckets, and a maximal coupling samples the published token exactly from the sender's private distribution.
notes: The receiver never sees the sender's model (pang_2026:asymmetric-setting-public-transcript).

name: Distribution copies
definition: Copies of the token distribution are made by rotating its intervals, and the message decides which copy the token is sampled from.

name: Feedback (posterior-matching) coding
definition: Every generated token is observed by both parties, so generation is a channel with noiseless feedback and each token guides the next embedding step.
notes: BAM also uses an optimal-transport coupling per token (guo_2026:ot-coupling-sampler).

name: Key-correlated sampling randomness
definition: The model's sampling randomness is correlated with a secret key instead of its distribution being changed, and the watermark is extended to carry a payload.
notes: Decoding uses only the key and the response (zamir_2024:decoder-distribution-agnostic).

name: Token-partition (red-green) watermark codes
definition: The message seeds or selects a split of tokens into favoured and disfavoured sets, biasing sampling, and the decoder picks the message whose split scores highest.
notes: Biases the distribution, so it does not preserve it.

name: Estimate-and-sample universal stegosystem
definition: The unknown cover distribution is estimated and stegotext is sampled from the estimate using the sender's private randomness.
notes: Estimation is by universal compression (heading of the claim).

name: Covert key establishment without a pre-shared secret
definition: Ciphertext under the recipient's public key, such as a session key, is carried in the cover, so parties who share no secret can still communicate covertly.
notes: Shares its grounding with m-public-key-block-parity.

name: Public-key ciphertext as block parity
definition: The message is encrypted under the recipient's public key and embedded as the parities of successive cover blocks.

name: Lattice key exchange in honest samples
definition: MLWE ciphertext coefficients are carried as small displacements in blocks that are honest samples from the sender's model, so that independently deployed agents agree a key.

name: Cover modification
definition: An existing cover is altered so that the alterations carry the message, exploiting limits of the warden such as human perception.

name: Keyed-set parity
definition: A pad or keystream selects a set of cover elements and each ciphertext bit is embedded as their parity.

name: Cost-based embedding
definition: Each modification of a cover element carries a cost, and the message is embedded under the conventional framework of distortion minimisation.
notes: No corpus quote defines lowest-cost embedding itself (Review A); the definition says only what the quote says.

name: Steganalyser-gradient cost adjustment
definition: Embedding costs are adjusted by the gradients of a target CNN steganalyser so that the stego image also fools it.

name: Repetition-rank block exchange
definition: In the ranking of a repetition-times compressor, a low-probability source block is kept or swapped for the block immediately following it, depending on the embedded bit.

name: Substitution codes
definition: An agreed or commonly known stand-in replaces a word, phrase, string or symbol in otherwise ordinary text, and which stand-in appears carries the message.
notes: Grounding partial: the quote covers synonym sets only; codewords, associated terms and character variants rest on their own leaves' quotes.

name: Synonym substitution
definition: Interchangeable synonyms form substitution sets, and the choice among them in a cover text carries the bits.
notes: The likeliest commentary scheme (Review A). Detected by m-text-feature-steganalysis.

name: Multi-base synonym coding
definition: Synonyms taken from WordNet are encoded by a multi-base coding method.
notes: Tlex; described by a survey, not verified from the original paper.

name: Vertex coding of synonyms
definition: Collected synonyms are encoded into unrepeated bit strings by vertex coding.
notes: Survey-described (Chang and Clark).

name: Matrix embedding over synonyms
definition: Matrix embedding raises embedding efficiency by reducing the number of synonym substitutions needed.
notes: Survey-described.

name: Syndrome-trellis-coded synonym substitution
definition: A double-layered syndrome-trellis code chooses the substitutions so as to minimise statistical and linguistic distortion.
notes: Survey-described.

name: Codeword substitution
definition: Agreed codewords, which need not be synonyms, stand in for the hidden states.
notes: Learned instance: skaf_2025:coinflip-arbitrary-codebook (R and L for Heads and Tails).

name: Associated-term substitution
definition: The payload is replaced by a closely associated term, such as the name of a product that implements it.
notes: Found in the corpus during this revision; neither review proposed it.

name: Character-variant substitution
definition: A variant character, such as a Unicode variant of an asterisk, replaces a string that a monitor penalises.

name: Surface-feature rule codes
definition: An explicit rule maps message symbols onto positional, countable or typographic features of the text, such as first letters, sentence lengths or punctuation.

name: Letter-position codes (acrostics)
definition: Message letters are placed at agreed positions, such as the first letter of each sentence, of alternate sentences or of every third word.
notes: The stride is a parameter, not a new mechanism. Chestega's player-name initials apply the same rule to entity names (desoky_2009:player-initial-codebook).

name: Initial-class codes
definition: The class of a token's initial letter (A-M against N-Z) carries a bit, rather than the letter itself.

name: Literal payload as a name or acronym
definition: The payload is written directly into the text as an imagined acronym or name.
notes: Not an acrostic: the letters are not spread over positions.

name: Count codes
definition: The count of some unit in successive segments of text (words or characters per sentence, letters per word), taken modulo the number of states, carries each state.
notes: Other counted units, such as sentences per comment, belong here by the reviewers' broadening (X), not by a source quote.

name: Word-length parity
definition: The parity of each word's length carries one bit.

name: Punctuation and special-character codes
definition: The choice of terminal punctuation, or of special characters inserted into the text, carries each state.

name: Surface-formatting codes
definition: Each formatting unit (a word, a whitespace run or a sentence) carries one symbol from the start of the answer, leaving the meaning of the text untouched.
notes: Schemes: capitalisation, markdown, whitespace, sentence markdown, sentence interjection, sentence newline (claim location field).

name: Overt encodings and ciphers
definition: The message is transformed by a standard encoding or cipher and written into the text, which hides its content but not that something is encoded.
notes: A landing class: an agent scheme that writes Base64 or a Caesar shift mimics these.

name: Byte encodings
definition: The message is written as Base64, UTF-8 binary or hexadecimal, possibly with bit swaps, rotations or repeated application.

name: Letter rotation and substitution ciphers
definition: Each letter is rotated by N places or replaced under a provided character mapping.

name: Partial word-level cipher
definition: Rot13 is applied to each word independently with probability p, interpolating between legible and fully enciphered text.

name: Enumerated-choice codes
definition: At each decision point the sender's rule yields a set of admissible alternatives, a bit string is assigned to each, and the one whose string matches the next data appears.

name: Move-choice indexing (ordered alternatives)
definition: A prearranged criterion orders a set of acceptable alternatives, and the index of the one played sends that value.
notes: Parent of the three move-choice leaves (user decision, 20261106). The leaves differ in how the acceptable set is cut: equal outcome, engine threshold, keyed strategy set.

name: Equivalent-alternative choice
definition: Among alternatives that can be shown not to change the outcome, the one played transmits information, and the receiver identifies which it was.
notes: A keyed generator fixes the value sent (murdoch_2004:keyed-generator-frequency-hopping). Simmons' subliminal channel (several ciphers decrypting to one message) is the cryptographic case.

name: Engine-ranked index
definition: A shared engine lists the moves scoring above a threshold T, sorts them by evaluation, and playing the i-th sends i.

name: Keyed strategy-set coding
definition: The set of best moves is permuted by a shared random number generator and seed, and message bits are consumed as an index into the permuted set.
notes: The permutation acts as a variable-length substitution cipher (ritchey_2012:substitution-and-sparse-use).

name: Mixed-radix index over all legal options
definition: Options at each position are sorted deterministically and each position is treated as a base-n digit, n being the number of options, until the message integer is consumed.
notes: Ignores option quality (barai_2026:uniform-legal-move-selection).

name: Combinatorial subset index
definition: A combinatorial number system converts the data into a choice of a set of units, and a target location for them can carry more.

name: Optional-insertion parameters
definition: Optional material added to a record (a variation in a played game) carries bits by where it begins, how long it is, and the choices within it.

name: Policy identity
definition: Each message symbol has its own agent, and the receiver decodes by identifying which agent produced the observed episode.

name: Signalling keyed by private knowledge
definition: Partners encode information in the plays they choose, and a secret they share but opponents lack (what each holds) acts as a key.
notes: Review A, gap 6.

name: Codebook choice
definition: An agreed table maps message values to a finite set of expressions, so that the one used codifies the bits.
notes: The grounding quote's expressions say the same thing; the children's need not (stated value, reference, utterance category).

name: Phrase codebook
definition: Each possible message is associated with a fixed phrase, such as an answer introduction, and the receiver finds which phrase was used.

name: Stated-value code
definition: The text states a number determined by the message, such as an age, and the receiver reads the integer and looks up its message.
notes: Not tied to the start of the text. An engine evaluation chosen from an agreed list lands here.

name: Reference code into shared data
definition: Message values are sent as references to items of shared data both parties hold, such as pointers to the words of a shared book.
notes: Shares its grounding with m-pointer-code. Chestega is placed here with partial evidence: desoky_2009:approach-chestega names chess data as the carrier, not the mapping; its target-square index is m-authentic-record-selection.

name: Reference to equally likely items
definition: A reference to one of many items both parties hold, each assumed equally likely (a verse of a shared book), leaves the covertext and stegotext distributions equal.
notes: Opening frequencies are Zipf-distributed (blasius_2009), so the uniformity condition fails for opening names.

name: Pointer (book-cipher) code
definition: Sender and receiver share a book and encipher the message as a series of pointers to its words.
notes: Review A, gap 3.

name: Utterance-category code
definition: The kind of remark made (a question, a complaint about the weather) stands for a message value, so the code is functional rather than lexical.
notes: Negotiated afresh for every shoe in the source.

name: Semantic-content choice
definition: The message selects what the generated text is about or does (its keywords, its semantic class, or the reasoning behaviour of a step) rather than its wording, and a model writes text with that content.
notes: Children ground keyword sets (wu_2024), ontology-entity classes (bai_2024) and reasoning behaviour (zhou_2026).

name: Keyword-set index
definition: Keyword sets are expanded by repeated sampling in proportion to probability, and the location index of each keyword in the expanded set encodes message bits.

name: Ontology-entity semantic space
definition: A semantic space is built from ontology-entity trees and secret messages are mapped onto it, without altering how the model samples.

name: Reasoning-behaviour choice
definition: Each reasoning step carries a bit in which high-level reasoning behaviour it shows rather than in its words.

name: Free choices within a task
definition: Choices a task leaves open, repetitive and supposedly arbitrary or unimportant ones such as variable names, serve as the carrier, the option taken carrying the information.
notes: Grounding partial: the quote names a kind of cover, not an encoding rule; compare the encode and decode operations with the child before any verdict. Move choice in quiet positions is related by reviewer inference, not by the source.

name: Item in/out bits
definition: The in/out choices of the first items of a task solution encode a number in binary, one bit per item (the knapsack cover).

name: Cover selection
definition: An unmodified object is chosen because its own attributes map to the message under an agreed rule.

name: Feature-hash selection
definition: Images in a database are indexed by hash sequences of their features, and images whose hashes equal the message segments are sent.

name: File-attribute category mapping
definition: Values of a file attribute are divided into categories, each mapped to a secret message, and files are chosen by category.
notes: Not image hashing (Review B).

name: Visual-word mapping
definition: Visual words extracted from images express the text to be hidden, and images containing them are selected.

name: Partial-duplicate patch retrieval
definition: Natural images sharing patches with a secret image are retrieved and sent, and the receiver stitches the patches back together.

name: Authentic-record selection
definition: Moves from unaltered, authenticated real games are chosen so that their data carry the message.
notes: Picking a real master game whose features carry the message lands here (Review A, restructure 4).

name: Generative synthesis of media
definition: A shared generator produces the container directly from the message, so no cover is modified, and an extractor recovers the message.

name: Message-to-latent mapping
definition: Secret bits are mapped to the generator's noise vector and a trained extractor recovers them from the generated image.

name: Latent search
definition: The generator's latent space is searched for the encoding whose output carries the message.

name: Secret-conditioned generator
definition: A secret block inside the generator writes the secret data into its feature maps during image generation.

name: Diffusion translation
definition: A pre-trained conditional diffusion model, with different conditions in its forward and backward processes, translates a secret image into a container without additional training.

name: Grille and inpainting
definition: A shared mask (a digital Cardan grille) marks where the message is written and a generator completes the rest of the image.

name: Generator-model database
definition: A database of generative models turns a secret image into an unrelated-looking image and back.

name: Generation-time watermark
definition: The mark is introduced while a generative model produces the image, through the model's parameters or its sampling input.
notes: Replaces the family tree's wm-generative-model definition, which excluded its own Tree-Ring child (Review B).

name: Fine-tuned decoder mark
definition: The latent decoder of a diffusion model is fine-tuned so that every generated image carries a fixed binary signature.

name: Initial-noise mark
definition: A pattern is written into the Fourier transform of the initial noise vector used for sampling, with no change to the model.

name: Learned media embedding
definition: Trainable networks hide data in an existing image or audio signal and recover it.
notes: Cover dependence, adversarial training and attack simulation are independent attributes, so a record may carry several (Review B).

name: Residual encoder
definition: The encoder outputs a residual image that is added back to the cover; the message enters as an extra input channel.

name: Cover-conditioned encoder
definition: The encoder takes the cover as well as the message, so the embedding depends on the cover; HiDDeN, for instance, concatenates the spatially replicated message to its intermediate representation of the cover.
notes: SteganoGAN quotes only the cover-and-message input (zhang_2019:approach-steganogan).

name: Cover-independent (universal) encoding
definition: The secret is encoded independently of the cover image.

name: Adversarially trained hiding
definition: Containers and covers are fed to an adversarial model, making training a three-player game.

name: Attack-simulated training
definition: Containers are distorted by simulated attacks during training before they reach the reveal network, so the mark survives them.

name: Physical-channel training
definition: The simulated distortions are those of real printing, display and photography.

name: Spectral speech hiding
definition: STFT and inverse-STFT layers inside the network let speech be hidden in speech.

name: Invertible encoder-decoder
definition: An invertible network performs encoding and decoding as reciprocal processes with shared parameters.

name: Adversarially trained text editing
definition: A jointly and adversarially trained encoder-decoder transformer takes a text and a binary message and outputs the text unobtrusively modified.
notes: Text carrier, learned mechanism.

name: Hyperbolic blending
definition: Message and carrier features are mapped to the Poincare ball, concatenated in the tangent space and mapped back to the ball.

name: Timing channels
definition: The times at which symbols are sent carry the information, not their content.
notes: Review A gap 2; Review B.

name: Move timing
definition: The sender delays making a move and the recipient measures the delay.
notes: Relevant only if the harness exposes timing to the receiver.

name: Collusion signals
definition: An agreed or salient feature of the input or of the output tells a colluding party when or how to act; often a one-bit message.
notes: 'How to act' covers signals that coordinate strategies (buscemi_2026:covert-communication-definition: "Such signals may function as implicit codes").

name: Input-feature trigger
definition: Both colluders misbehave only when an agreed feature is present in the input, so no message passes between them.
notes: Split from m-output-signal by both reviews. Non-landing by user decision (20261106).

name: Output signal
definition: The sender puts an agreed mark in its own output, such as a variable name or a loop form, so the receiver knows to act.
notes: Also mallen_2024:subversion-untrusted-monitoring-output-collusion (a fixed comment string).

name: Focal magic numbers
definition: A number made salient by world knowledge (a famous prime, a constant from a novel or a game) serves as the signal.
notes: Review A, gap 5.

name: Authenticate, then act
definition: Players covertly authenticate those they may collude with, then follow an algorithm that acts on the authentication so as to win the competition.

name: Payoff-anchored numeric signals
definition: Numeric messages reuse values drawn from the payoff structure of the game both parties play, converging on a compact, low-entropy set of signalling symbols.
notes: Under decimal communication. How the values map to strategies is not given (buscemi_2026:partially-covert-opacity), so the node fixes the symbol inventory, not a decoding rule.

name: Coordination without a message
definition: Parties collude or coordinate their actions, whether or not they communicate with each other; the distinction between explicit and tacit collusion may break down for agents.
notes: How a scheme was agreed is recorded as acquisition = focal; the code itself is classified in its own class. Non-landing by user decision (20261106).

name: Schelling-point choice of scheme
definition: Of the many possible schemes, some are salient (named in the prompt, in a shared file system, common in training), and isolated parties converge on them.
notes: Non-landing (both reviews): it records how a scheme was chosen; record acquisition = focal.

name: Conventions emerging in interaction
definition: Agents exchange symbols with no predefined interpretation, and any meaning emerges endogenously through interaction.
notes: Records how meaning arose. Buscemi's payoff-anchored code is m-payoff-anchored-symbols. Non-landing by user decision (20261106).

name: Learned tacit collusion
definition: Algorithms adapt their strategies to collude through interaction, without the parties communicating.
notes: Non-landing (both reviews): nothing is sent or hidden. The pricing quote does not name the learning method.

name: Out-of-band physical signals
definition: An agreed physical act outside the moves of the game carries the information.
notes: Shares its grounding with m-orientation-signal.

name: Orientation signal
definition: The orientation in which an object is placed (a card led horizontally or vertically) carries the information.

name: Acoustic signal
definition: A sound, or its absence, relays the information.

name: Security definitions, limits and capacity laws
definition: Definitions of undetectability and results on how much can be hidden; no scheme is judged against them.

name: Information-theoretic security
definition: Detection is a hypothesis test, and security is the relative entropy between cover and stego distributions.

name: Complexity-theoretic security
definition: Security is computational indistinguishability; one-way functions suffice for secure steganography.

name: Capacity laws
definition: Under stated assumptions (covers of uniform capacity, a quantitative steganalyser) and asymptotically, secure capacity grows only as the square root of the number of covers.
notes: Conditional, not unrestricted (Review B).

name: Informal limits and terminology
definition: A survey-level account of what steganography is and can do.

name: Evaluations, benchmarks and elicitation conditions
definition: Frameworks and conditions that measure or elicit hiding, or classify risks, rather than hide anything.

name: Evaluation frameworks
definition: Software frameworks and decompositions that organise capability measurement.

name: Encoded message-passing task
definition: An encoder hides a secret message in its answer to a cover task for a decoder copy of itself, while a monitor judges suspicion.

name: Encoded reasoning task
definition: Models are evaluated on encoding their reasoning.

name: Control evaluations
definition: Protocols meant to stay safe despite intentional subversion are evaluated.

name: Stateless subversion evaluation
definition: Systems must generate and act on their own strategies for subverting control protocols without shared memory between contexts.

name: Agentic stegosystem construction
definition: A tool-using agent must build a working natural-language stegosystem.
notes: The system built is Zamir's (m-pseudorandom-watermark-code).

name: Focal-point evaluations
definition: Studies of how, when and why focal points emerge in models, compared with humans.

name: Focality prompts
definition: A prompt tells the model which kind of salience to aim at.
notes: An elicitation condition (Review B), not a hiding scheme.

name: Scheme-discovery condition
definition: The model is asked to think of a scheme for the task, use it, and later re-derive it to decode.
notes: Replaces lgt-model-devised. Whoever devised a scheme, the scheme itself is classified by its mechanism.

name: Training-based elicitation
definition: RL fine-tuning against a task reward and a monitor penalty is used to induce or study hidden encoding.

name: Collusion audits and benchmarks
definition: Frameworks that audit collusion through outcome metrics and conversation logs.

name: Risk taxonomies
definition: Multi-agent risks are sorted into failure modes and risk factors.

name: Detectors, monitors and defences
definition: Methods that detect, measure, remove or read hidden communication.

name: Statistical feature steganalysis
definition: Statistical attacks detect significant deviations from a model of the cover caused by inserting hidden data.

name: Text feature steganalysis
definition: Semantic features of word choice, such as synonym context fitness, feed a classifier.

name: Game-statistics attacks
definition: Game length, playing level and result are tested for deviations caused by embedding.

name: Entropy of non-text messages
definition: Covert messages are detected by their lower entropy than random baselines.
notes: Review A, gap 10.

name: LLM classifiers
definition: A fine-tuned LLM judges whether a text carries hidden data.

name: Prompted LLM monitor
definition: A model given the cover task and answer, but not the secret, is told to rate suspicion, and a threshold set at a fixed false-positive rate decides.
notes: Both reviews; the opposing team's main tool in hypersteg.

name: Active-warden defences
definition: The overseer rewrites the message, for example by paraphrasing it while keeping its meaning, to destroy any payload instead of only detecting it.

name: Activation probes
definition: Probes on hidden states reconstruct the secret or read deception, calibrated to a false-positive rate.

name: Concept-lens readout
definition: Concepts read through a Jacobian lens are compared across agents to find colluding pairs.

name: Game-record inference
definition: An inference engine analyses the bidding and play in complete game records to detect collusive play.

name: Hypothesis-comparison forensics
definition: The hypothesis that a specified method was used to transmit information is weighed against the hypothesis that it was not.

name: Decision-theoretic utility gap
definition: Steganography is measured by comparing the downstream utility of a message to parties who can and cannot decode it.

name: Adversary decoding attempts
definition: Near-copies of the decoder, trained with minor variations, try to recover the message rather than just flag it.
notes: Review A, gap 11.

name: Non-steganographic foundations
definition: Work on chess language, chess play, human move choice, hyperbolic geometry and coordination learning that hides nothing.

name: Chess language models and datasets
definition: Models trained on chess games paired with chess text.

name: Commentary generation
definition: Neural systems that generate commentary text for chess moves.
notes: No engine input required (Review B).

name: Commentary evaluation
definition: An LLM evaluates chess commentary.

name: Models of human move choice
definition: Models of chess skill measured by the quality of the moves played.
notes: Candidate cover distributions or warden models for move-choice channels.

name: Intrinsic rating models
definition: Formulas represent playing strength by the quality of moves played, fitted by regression.

name: Engine-match assessment
definition: Whether a player's move matches an engine's choice is counted, and this can detect or be gamed by cheaters.

name: Neural human-move predictors
definition: Networks trained on human games predict the move a human played.

name: Engine and opening analysis
definition: Engines and game databases measure opening diversity or variant balance.

name: LLM chess play
definition: Benchmarks of how well language models play chess.

name: Hyperbolic embeddings and measurement
definition: Data are embedded in hyperbolic space to represent hierarchy.

name: Hyperbolic network layers and agents
definition: Neural network operations defined in hyperbolic geometry.

name: Symmetry-robust coordination learning
definition: Self-play against randomly relabelled, symmetry-equivalent copies of the partner, so agents coordinate with partners they have not met.
notes: A coordination method, not a hiding scheme.
